g: A figure or mark in the shape of the letter Y.
A Y-shaped object, such as a railroad fork or a support for a telescope; a wye, a bifurcation.
(lepidopterology) A moth of the genus Plusia, having markings resembling the letter Y.
(Canada, US, informal) A particular facility run by the YMCA/YWCA.
A Y-shaped bone forming part of the rib cage of certain fish.
A forked cable typically used to split or recombine audiovisual signals.
(genetics) A mammalian sex chromosome: in the XY sex-determination system, cells of females typically have a pair of X chromosomes, while cells of males typically have an X and a Y.
The electric current through one branch of the star arrangement of a three-phase circuit.
A Welsh cheese consisting of cheddar blended with mustard seed and ale.
A surveyor's instrument for measuring differences of level by means of a telescope resting in a Y-shaped support.
A kind of theodolite shaped like the capital letter Y.
(informal, dialect, subject pronoun) you; ya; ye.
The group spoken or written to.
I need y'all help for a minute.

(informal, now chiefly Southern US, African-American Vernacular, New York Latino English, Appalachia, Caribbean, Indian South African English, Māori English, Singapore, Newfoundland and Labrador) You (plural).
(chiefly Southern US, African-American Vernacular, in greetings) Everyone; everybody.
I made this for both y'all and your wife to enjoy.
(slang, Southern US) Bigotry and intolerance are unacceptable; no one should be discriminated against.
A modern outgrowth of traditional country music that incorporates elements of rock while keeping the country twanginess.
(US, Southern US, Appalachia, informal) you hear; used as a tag question or to strengthen a command, warning, or statement.
(informal) Shortened form of you see (meaning you comprehend).

(algebraic geometry) The axis on a graph that is usually drawn from bottom to top and usually shows the range of values of variable dependent on one other variable, or the second of two independent variables.
(algebraic geometry) The direction aligned with the y-axis of a coordinate system.
(clothing) (of briefs) With a flap at the front framed by Y-shaped seams.
(UK) Having a Y-shaped seam, as Y-fronts do.
(plural only, UK, Ireland, Commonwealth, informal) Briefs that have a fly as part of an inverted Y formed by the seams.
(mathematics) A point at which a line crosses the y-axis of a Cartesian grid.
A splitter; a device used to split a single jack into two.
A three-way intersection of routes shaped like a capital letter Y.
A similarly shaped section in a pipe, etc.
(behavioral science) A variant of the T-maze, having the junction shaped like the letter Y.
An immunoglobulin is a large, Y-shaped protein.
(humorous) An imaginary coffin in the shape of a capital letter Y, supposedly used for burying a sexually promiscuous woman.
A splitter; a device used to split a single power source into two.
A convention whereby Esperanto’s circumflex accents (ĉ, ĝ, ĥ, ĵ, ŝ, ŭ) are replaced by an y after the non-diacriticked letter (cy, gy, hy, jy, sy, uy), for convenience of typing.
(sudoku) A three-cell combination in a sudoku grid which allows the elimination of a candidate in a fourth cell.
Any word starting with Y considered to be taboo in the given context, such as Yid, yobo or yokel.
